item.title: What Burndown Charts Miss About Real Software Delivery
item.content:encoded: This article argues that common software-delivery metrics such as burndown charts, velocity tracking, and percentage-complete estimates misrepresent how software is actually built. Because development is exploratory, nonlinear, and shaped by discovery, the author contends that demos, narratives, and shipped outcomes provide a more accurate picture of progress than process metrics designed primarily for reporting and stakeholder communication

item.title: Platform Engineering Will Eat Software Engineering and That's a Good Thing
item.content:encoded: This article argues that platform engineering is evolving from a specialized infrastructure discipline into the context in which modern software development happens. As AI workloads, internal developer platforms, and self-service infrastructure become essential to product delivery, platform teams increasingly determine what organizations can build and ship. The author contends that platform engineering now has direct business impact and should be viewed as a strategic function rather than a support role.

item.title: How to Architect a Scalable AI Tech Stack
item.content:encoded: This article provides an overview of the modern AI tech stack, breaking it down into data, model, and application layers. It explores the infrastructure required to build, deploy, and maintain AI systems, with particular attention to Generative AI, vector databases, MLOps tooling, model serving, and cloud-native architectures. The guide also examines emerging trends such as multimodal AI, edge deployment, AutoML, and responsible AI practices.

item.title: Your MVP Is Probably Too Big
item.content:encoded: Building a smaller MVP is not about cutting corners. It is about testing one real assumption before you build everything else. Most founders overbuild because launching something small feels uncomfortable, not because the extra features are actually needed. If you removed half your planned features and the core promise still held up, you probably should.

item.title: Faster Code Generation Doesn't Guarantee Faster Software Delivery
item.content:encoded: AI Coding Assistants can help developers write code faster, but real team speed depends on review quality, code ownership, testing habits, and clear workflow rules.

item.title: The Radiology Shortage Is a Coordination Problem Disguised as a Hiring Problem
item.content:encoded: Radiology is still organized around a one-study, one-radiologist workflow that no longer scales with growing imaging demand and rising complexity. Other industries solved similar problems by shifting from individual execution to coordinated infrastructure. The future of radiology may depend less on adding more specialists and more on redesigning how diagnostic work is distributed, reviewed, and assembled.

item.title: 7 of the Best Voice Agent Testing Platforms in 2026
item.content:encoded: 42% of voice agent failures happen at the audio layer – invisible to generic LLM evals. This guide compares seven platforms built to test what transcript-only evaluation misses. Pick based on your build stage, not hype.

item.title: What Production-Grade RAG Evaluation Should Look Like
item.content:encoded: This article argues that evaluating agentic RAG systems requires far more than a single faithfulness score. It explores a production-focused evaluation stack built around RAGAS component metrics, node-level observability with LangSmith and Langfuse, critic scoring, retrieval-round analysis, latency and cost monitoring, and carefully curated evaluation datasets. The central thesis is that modern RAG systems fail in many ways that end-to-end metrics alone cannot detect.

item.title: Deploying On-Device AI Guardrails With Docker 29.1 and Spanner Omni
item.content:encoded: Shifting AI to the edge solves latency and privacy issues but creates a governance nightmare. This technical deep dive explores how backend engineers can use Docker Engine 29.1 and Google Spanner Omni to run SLMs locally, enforce strict Java-based safety guardrails, and maintain globally synchronized compliance logs.

item.title: The Cloud Data Leak: Architecting SQL to Stop Financial Bleeding
item.content:encoded: Cloud storage may be cheap, but processing, moving, and managing data often isn't. This article examines seven common architectural patterns that inflate cloud bills, including small-file fragmentation, cross-region joins, excessive retention windows, poor storage tiering, and unrestricted queries. It argues that modern data engineers must think like FinOps practitioners, optimizing not just for performance and scale but also for long-term infrastructure economics.

item.title: The Math Behind RevShare vs Flat-Fee Partner Compensation (And Why Most Teams Model It Wrong)
item.content:encoded:
Every partner program must choose between CPA (flat fee per conversion), RevShare (percentage of ongoing revenue), or a hybrid. This isn't a business call — it's an engineering decision that shapes your commission engine, billing logic, and financial edge cases. CPA is predictable but decouples partner incentives from customer quality. RevShare aligns incentives but compounds costs over time and introduces negative balance carryover — a policy decision with massive financial impact. The crossover point (the customer lifetime at which RevShare total commission equals the CPA) is the single most important number in your model. This article provides the Python models, crossover calculation, and the framework for building real-time comparison into your system.

item.title: Why Server-to-Server Tracking Replaced Pixels — And What Breaks When You Get It Wrong
item.content:encoded:
S2S (postback) tracking replaces browser-dependent pixels with direct server-to-server HTTP calls for conversion attribution. The concept is four steps: generate a click ID, store it, fire a postback on conversion, attribute the commission. The implementation is where it breaks. Five failure modes hit every production setup: click ID evaporation (the ID doesn't survive the user journey), postback delivery failure (the HTTP request never arrives), duplicate fires (the affiliate gets paid twice), parameter mismatches (the systems disagree on field names), and timing issues (sessions expire before conversion). This article covers the protocol-level mechanics, production code patterns for each failure mode, and why monitoring is the actual product — not the tracking setup itself.

item.title: Most Node.js Apps Using ClamAV Have the Same Bug. Here's What It Is.
item.content:encoded:
Calling ClamAV from Node.js looks easy: spawn clamscan, check the exit code, done. But the standard implementation has a silent bug — exit code 2 means "scan could not complete," not "clean," and almost every custom wrapper collapses it into one of the other two outcomes. The result is a false-clean verdict on encrypted archives, permission-denied files, and timeouts. The fix is to model ClamAV's three real outcomes — Clean, Malicious, ScanError — as three explicit return values, and force the caller to handle ScanError as a security decision rather than a programming error. This article explains why this matters, what the failure looks like in production, and what a correct minimal wrapper looks like in practice.
